Kyrgyz Metals & Mining Firms Reel as Debt Crisis Deepens

BISHKEK, June 14—Kyrgyzstan’s metals and mining industry is facing mounting turmoil as a deepening debt crisis triggers production cuts, project delays, and warnings of possible layoffs, industry officials said Friday.

The crisis erupted last month after a sharp tightening of credit conditions, leaving several mining companies unable to refinance maturing loans or secure new working capital. The situation has been exacerbated by falling global prices for key exports such as gold and antimony, shrinking revenues across the sector.

Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC, the country’s largest gold producer, confirmed it has suspended exploration work at two sites and is operating its main refinery at reduced capacity. “We are in active discussions with lenders and the government to stabilize our operations,” said a company spokesperson. “Our immediate priority is to protect jobs and maintain production where possible.”

At least three other major mining firms, including Altai Resources and Talas Mining Group, have announced temporary shutdowns or reduced shifts, union representatives told reporters. According to the Kyrgyz Mining Association, sector-wide output fell 18% in May compared to a year earlier.

“The credit freeze has hit smaller operators particularly hard, with some already defaulting on payments to suppliers and contractors,” said Bakyt Sariyev, an industry analyst in Bishkek. “Unless liquidity returns soon, more companies could face insolvency.”

Government officials said emergency talks with industry leaders were ongoing, but warned that a rapid solution was unlikely. “We are monitoring the situation closely,” Deputy Mining Minister Nurlan Mambetov stated. “Our goal is to preserve the integrity of the sector during this challenging period.”
